newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia offers practice in sea mine clearing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia offers practice in sea mine clearing.

text.p: Indonesia and Singapore are cooperating in clearing the seaways of World War Two mines and Jakarta has offered other nations practice in mine sweeping, the official Antara news agency reported on Friday.

It quoted Indonesia's Navy Chief of Staff Vice Admiral Arief Kushariadi as saying on Thursday that thousands of mines from World War Two could still be found in waters around the archipelago, straddling the equator across Southeast Asia for some 5,000 km (3,000 miles).
"The number of the mines reaches thousands and they are still dangerous," he said.
Antara quoted Kushariadi as saying mines were found in the Java Sea and also in waters around Irian Jaya and other regions considered strategic by former Allied and Japanese forces.
